audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph first ark-transfer attempt and Uzzah death, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed against 2 Samuel 6 for leadership consultation, broad consent, cart transport, animal stumble, Uzzah's intervention and death, David's anger and fear, Obed-edom's household, and blessing language.

verses.restored: David consulted with commanders of thousands and hundreds and with every leader.

familiar.text: And David consulted with the captains of thousands and hundreds, and with every leader.

verses.restored: David said to all assembly of Israel, If it seems good to you and comes from YHWH our Divine, let us send widely to our relatives remaining throughout lands of Israel, and with them priests and Levites in their cities and pasturelands, that they may gather to us.

familiar.text: And David said unto all the congregation of Israel, If it seem good unto you, and that it be of the LORD our God, let us send abroad unto our brethren every where, that are left in all the land of Israel, and with them also to the priests and Levites which are in their cities and suburbs, that they may gather themselves unto us:

verses.restored: Let us bring ark of our Divine back to us, for we did not seek it in days of Saul.

familiar.text: And let us bring again the ark of our God to us: for we enquired not at it in the days of Saul.

verses.restored: All assembly said to do so, for matter was right in eyes of all people.

familiar.text: And all the congregation said that they would do so: for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.

verses.restored: David gathered all Israel from Shihor of Egypt to entrance of Hamath to bring ark of Divine from Kiriath-jearim.

familiar.text: So David gathered all Israel together, from Shihor of Egypt even unto the entering of Hemath, to bring the ark of God from Kirjathjearim.

verses.restored: David and all Israel went up to Baalah, Kiriath-jearim of Judah, to bring from there ark of Divine, YHWH enthroned upon cherubim, whose name is called upon it.

familiar.text: And David went up, and all Israel, to Baalah, that is, to Kirjathjearim, which belonged to Judah, to bring up thence the ark of God the LORD, that dwelleth between the cherubims, whose name is called on it.

verses.restored: They carried ark of Divine on a new cart from house of Abinadab; Uzzah and Ahio guided cart.

familiar.text: And they carried the ark of God in a new cart out of the house of Abinadab: and Uzza and Ahio drave the cart.

verses.restored: David and all Israel celebrated before Divine with all strength, with songs, lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.

familiar.text: And David and all Israel played before God with all their might, and with singing, and with harps, and with psalteries, and with timbrels, and with cymbals, and with trumpets.

verses.restored: When they came to threshing floor of Chidon, Uzzah reached out his hand to hold ark, because oxen stumbled.

familiar.text: And when they came unto the threshingfloor of Chidon, Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled.

verses.restored: Anger of YHWH burned against Uzzah, and YHWH struck him because he reached his hand to ark; he died there before Divine.

familiar.text: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he put his hand to the ark: and there he died before God.

verses.restored: David was angry because YHWH had broken out in a breach against Uzzah; that place is called Perez-uzzah to this day.

familiar.text: And David was displeased, because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzza: wherefore that place is called Perezuzza to this day.

verses.restored: David feared Divine that day, saying, How shall I bring ark of Divine to me?

familiar.text: And David was afraid of God that day, saying, How shall I bring the ark of God home to me?

verses.restored: David did not bring ark to himself into city of David but turned it aside to house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

familiar.text: So David brought not the ark home to himself to the city of David, but carried it aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite.

verses.restored: Ark of Divine remained with household of Obed-edom in his house three months, and YHWH blessed household of Obed-edom and all he had.

familiar.text: And the ark of God remained with the family of Obededom in his house three months. And the LORD blessed the house of Obededom, and all that he had.

translation_notes: Unanimous approval by leaders and assembly does not prove a plan is safe. Consensus can coexist with missing expertise and unclear responsibility.
Priests and Levites are invited to gather, but the narrative does not show them directing the transport method; later blame must not erase David's leadership role.
The new cart and stumbling oxen expose a systems and transport-safety failure. Animals are participants affected by human planning, not props.
Uzzah reaches to prevent the ark from falling. His death is sacred violence and must not be explained by claiming he had a corrupt heart.
The episode may not be used to frighten children, disabled people, religious workers, or anyone who makes an emergency intervention.
David's anger at the breach is preserved; protest and fear before a violent sacred tradition need not be suppressed.
Obed-edom's household receives the ark after a death. They must not be treated as a disposable test site or containment zone.
No one should imitate ark handling, dangerous processions, or emergency behavior based on this narrative.
safety_note: Do not use Uzzah's death to justify fear-based religion, victim-blaming, unsafe ritual practice, leader immunity, or claims that accidental contact deserves death. Center Uzzah's protective action, failed planning, animal safety, David's responsibility, and Obed-edom's household consent.
